record.synthesis_method: ball milling followed by heat treatment
record.evidence_quote: Substituting Sb with Si significantly increases the ionic conductivity, with Li6.6 Si0.6 Sb0.4 S5 I reaching 9.9 × 10−3 S cm−1 at 25 ◦ C.
record.notes: Activation energy 0.18 eV is from the same Arrhenius fit (quoted in Section 2.2: 'The activation energies are 0.28 eV for Li6 SbS5 I, 0.18 eV for Li6.6 Si0.6 Sb0.4 S5 I, and 0.23 eV for Li6.75 Si0.75 Sb0.25 S5 I'). Conductivity is from the fitted bulk-plus-grain-boundary resistance RSE, not separated; kind recorded as unspecified. Sintering field holds the 450 °C annealing temperature; the paper calls it heat treatment/annealing. Relative density not given for this composition.
